oligos.indication: Homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia (HoFH); severe heterozygous FH / severe hypercholesterolaemia
oligos.developer: Isis Pharmaceuticals (IND sponsorship transferred to Genzyme Corporation, 23 Jul 2008 - S1 regulatory history)
oligos.max_phase: Phase 3 completed; NDA 203568 under FDA review in S1/S2. EU application received a CHMP negative opinion (S4: 'in the view of the CHMP's negative opinion for Kynamro'). US approval status is not asserted from these documents.
oligos.sequence_locus: S4 kynamro_AR PDF p.10, section 2.2.2 'Active Substance' - the sequence is published only as the IUPAC/9CI chemical name (quoted verbatim in sequence_5to3_asprinted), not as a letter string. Residue-by-residue reading of that name gives the 20 bases above.
oligos.sugar_modifications: 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl) (2'-MOE) ribose at positions 1-5 and 16-20; 2'-deoxyribose (DNA) at positions 6-15. Read residue-by-residue from the chemical name in S4 p.10.
oligos.gapmer_design: 5-10-5 (5 x 2'-MOE wing / 10 x DNA gap / 5 x 2'-MOE wing), read from the chemical name in S4 p.10; S1 p.29 calls mipomersen a 'second-generation 2'-methoxyethyl (MOE) gapmer antisense inhibitor'.
oligos.conjugate: NOT_REPORTED (no conjugate described in any of the five documents)
oligos.purity_method: NOT_REPORTED (S4 p.11 describes liquid chromatography purification in the manufacturing process but prints no purity specification or value)
oligos.identity_confirmation: S4 p.10: 'The chemical structure of mipomersen has been confirmed using several techniques which include nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), mass spectrometry, complement hybridization, elemental analysis and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR).'
oligos.synthesis_platform: S4 p.11: four-operation process - 'computer-controlled solid-phase synthesis (the nucleotide assembly of mipomersen), liquid chromatography purification, final deprotection and precipitation, and isolation of the drug substance by freeze drying.'
oligos.notes: Molecular formula C230H305N67 O122 P19 S19 Na19, MW 7594.9 g/mol (S4 p.9). S4 p.10 states 'mipomersen contains 19 phosphorothioate diester linkages, the drug substance is a mixture of 2^19 diastereoisomers' - independently fixing the length at 20 nt and the backbone as fully phosphorothioate. PARSING HAZARD: the chemical name as printed in the EMA PDF contains a run-together token 'm5CT' where every other residue is hyphen-separated; it is resolved here as m5C followed by T because (a) 'm5CT' is not a valid single residue designation and (b) that resolution is the only one giving 20 residues / 19 internucleotide linkages, matching the stated P19 S19 formula and the stated 19 PS linkages. This is a documented resolution of a typographical defect in the source, not an inferred sequence. Neither FDA review (S1, S2) prints the sequence.

oligos.target_gene: SMN2 (intron splicing silencer N1 / ISS-N1 in the intron downstream of exon 7 of the SMN2 pre-mRNA)
oligos.developer: Ionis/Isis Pharmaceuticals (originator of ISIS 396443) with Biogen as applicant
oligos.max_phase: Approved in the EU - S5 p.6/p.8: CHMP recommended and the European Commission granted a marketing authorisation to Spinraza on 21 April 2017. S3 is the FDA NDA 209531 review supporting the US application.
oligos.sequence_locus: S5 spinraza_AR PDF p.12, section 2.2.2 'Active Substance' ('consisting of 18 nucleotide residues with the sequence 5'-MeUMeCAMeCMeUMeUMeUMeCAMeUAAMeUGMeCMeUGG-3''), corroborated residue-by-residue by the full chemical name printed immediately below it on the same page.
oligos.sugar_modifications: Uniformly 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl) (2'-MOE) at all 18 positions - S5 p.12 'a uniformly modified 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl) phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide'.
oligos.gapmer_design: NOT_APPLICABLE (uniformly 2'-MOE modified splice-switching ASO; no DNA gap)
oligos.conjugate: NOT_REPORTED (no conjugate described in any of the five documents)
oligos.purity_method: S5 p.20: active substance specification includes 'purity (Full Length n) (IP-HPLC-UV-MS)'; no numeric specification is printed.
oligos.identity_confirmation: S5 p.19: structure elucidation by 'nuclear magnetic resonance (1H NMR, 13C NMR, 31P NMR) spectroscopy, mass spectrometry (MS)'; routine identity by IP-HPLC-UV-MS.
oligos.synthesis_platform: S5 p.19-20: 'Solid-phase synthesis (production of crude intermediate)' followed by purification; the coupling chemistry 'is not stereospecific producing a mixture of two stereoisomers at each linkage'.
oligos.notes: Molecular formula C234H323N61O128P17S17Na17, relative molecular mass 7501.0 g/mol (S5 p.12) - the P17 S17 fixes 17 phosphorothioate linkages across an 18-mer. 'Me' in the printed sequence denotes 5-methyl (5-methylcytidine and 5-methyluridine), confirmed residue-by-residue by the chemical name on the same page. NOTE a quality-section inconsistency in S5 itself: p.11 (section 2.2.1) describes the active substance as 'the sodium salt of a 18-mer 2'-O-methyl-phosphothioate oligoribonucleotide' whereas p.12 (section 2.2.2) and the chemical name give 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl); the 2'-MOE description is the one supported by the chemical name and molecular formula. S3 (FDA) states only '18-mer 2'-MOE phosphorothioate antisense oligonucleotide' and does not print the sequence.

measurements.verbatim_quote: In the Phase 1 trial ISIS 301012-CS1, transient, reversible, dose-dependent increases within the normal range in aPTT were observed. measurements.n_subjects: 261 mipomersen; 129 placebo (arm sizes from Table 49 on the same page: 'TOTAL Mipo (N=261)', 'TOTAL Placebo (N=129)')
measurements.control_description: Placebo group mean change from baseline to Week 28/ET in the same pooled Phase 3 analysis
measurements.effect_vs_control: Mean change -0.93 (mipomersen) vs 0.00 (placebo); the reviewer states there were no clinically notable differences between the treatment groups
measurements.severity_stated_by_source: no clinically notable differences between the treatment groups
measurements.source_locus: S1 fda_kynamro_mipomersen_203568_MedR.pdf PDF p.187 (printed p.186), section 7.4.2 laboratory findings narrative preceding Table 49 (Reference ID 3221077)
measurements.verbatim_quote: For coagulation parameters, there were no clinically notable differences between the treatment groups in the pooled Phase 3 trials,  ISIS 301012-CS5 (patients with HoFH), or ISIS 301012-CS6 with respect to mean changes in aPTT, INR and PT from baseline to Week 28/ET.  For the pooled Phase 3 groups, the mean change from baseline to Week 28/ET in coagulation parameters were as follows: • The mean change in aPTT was -0.93 secs in the mipomersen group and 0.00 sec in the placebo group. • The mean change in INR was 0.02 in the mipomersen group and 0.04 in the placebo group. • The mean change in prothrombin time (PT) was 0.01 sec in the mipomersen group and 0.25 sec in the placebo group.
measurements.notes: MEASURED NULL with numbers (absence row of the strongest kind: a real per-arm mean change, not silence). Note the paradox worth preserving: the aPTT mean change is slightly NEGATIVE (-0.93 s) at the chronic SC 200 mg/week dose, i.e. the acute IV aPTT prolongation seen in Phase 1 does not carry over to steady-state weekly SC dosing. Section 7.3.5.7 of the same review makes the same statement: 'In the pooled Phase 3 clinical trials, the aPTT, INR, and PT from baseline to Week 28/ET did not show any meaningful differences between the placebo and mipomersen groups.'

measurements.notes: REGULATORY SILENCE ROW - the EMA assessment report for Spinraza contains ZERO occurrences of 'aPTT', 'thromboplastin', 'prothrombin' or 'INR' (verified by grep over the whole 117-page text: aPTT count = 0). The CHMP handled coagulation entirely as an ANTISENSE CLASS risk carried across from other compounds, listing 'Thrombocytopenia and coagulation abnormalities' as an Important potential risk managed by SmPC section 4.4 wording alone, with no additional pharmacovigilance activity. This is a striking divergence from the FDA, which built a named section (8.4.6.3) around the 19% aPTT shift and required coagulation testing before every maintenance dose. Divergence of two regulators on the same dossier - record it, do not average it. effect_direction is NOT_REPORTED because nothing was measured, not 'no_change'.

QUOTE CONVENTION. Every verbatim_quote is copied character-for-character from the document text with two mechanical normalizations and nothing else: (1) PDF line-wrap whitespace joined to single spaces, and (2) curly quotes and primes left as the document renders them. Superscript footnote reference numbers are RETAINED as printed digits, which is why two quotes read 'only in Study CS2,37 which includes' and 'lumbar puncture.96 These events included' - the 37 and 96 are the review's footnote markers, not part of the sentence. No word, number or unit has been altered, and no ellipsis hides an intervening clause except where the quote is drawn from a table, in which case the row labels and their cells are reproduced in printed column order. Where a sentence straddles a page break (the mipomersen-warfarin sentence, which begins 'Co-administration of mipomersen with' at the foot of S1 PDF p.46), the quote starts at the top of the following page rather than silently splicing across the intervening page header - the omitted opening words are recorded in source_locus.

CONTRADICTIONS AND HAZARDS FOUND
1. Nusinersen, EMA vs FDA. The EMA assessment report for Spinraza (S5) contains ZERO occurrences of 'aPTT', 'thromboplastin', 'prothrombin' or 'INR' across all 117 pages (verified by grep). The CHMP treated coagulation purely as an antisense CLASS risk carried over from other compounds, listed 'Thrombocytopenia and coagulation abnormalities' as an Important potential risk managed by SmPC section 4.4 wording alone, and required pre-lumbar-puncture testing only 'in case of risk factors'. The FDA, on the same dossier, built a named section around a 19% aPTT shift and required coagulation testing before EVERY maintenance dose. Two regulators, one dossier, opposite conclusions about how much coagulation data exists. Both positions are recorded as separate rows; do not reconcile or average them.
2. Nusinersen, protocol vs practice. The CS3B protocol DID list coagulation tests - the Clinical Review (S3 PDF p.166) lists '• Coagulation: aPTT, PT, and INR' among the CS3B safety laboratory tests - yet the Clinical Safety Review (S3 PDF p.58) lists as a deficiency that 'Coagulation laboratory parameters were measured post-baseline only in Study CS2'. Planned is not performed. The controlled trial therefore produced no post-baseline coagulation data at all, which is why the 19% aPTT figure has no comparator.
3. Nusinersen, SM201 denominator. S5 PDF p.87 says 'Five subjects (25%)' had LP-related AEs in Study SM201; S5 PDF p.90 says 'Five subjects (29%)' for the same study with the same event list. 25% implies n=20 (the AR gives 20 on p.87), 29% implies n=17. Numerator agrees, denominator does not. Flagged in the row, not resolved.
4. Mipomersen, acute vs chronic. Phase 1 IV dosing produced a clear dose-dependent aPTT rise at Cmax (200 mg: 30.6 -> 35.7 s; 400 mg: 26.0 -> 38.0 s) that was ABSENT after subcutaneous dosing and gone by 24 h; chronic 200 mg/week SC dosing in Phase 3 produced a mean aPTT change of -0.93 s, i.e. slightly negative. The aPTT signal is a Cmax/route phenomenon, not a cumulative one. Anyone pooling 'mipomersen aPTT' across routes will manufacture a false null or a false positive depending on the mix.
5. Mipomersen, PT internal tension. Section 7.3.5.7 reports that 17 of 141 (12.1%) subjects in the CS6 open-label extension had PT > 1.2 x baseline, with 2 crossing the protocol rule (PT > 20 s or INR > 1.5), while Table 49 shows the AE 'Prothrombin time prolonged' was LESS frequent on mipomersen (1/261, 0.4%) than on placebo (2/129, 1.6%) in the controlled Phase 3 set, and the pooled Phase 3 mean PT change was +0.01 s. Short controlled exposure and long open-label exposure disagree. Both are recorded.
6. Mipomersen, denominators outside the coagulation section. Section 7.3.5.7 prints percentages without denominators. The 141 (CS6 treated) and 39 (CS6 HoFH) denominators come from elsewhere in the same review (S1 PDF p.70 and p.90) and reproduce the printed percentages exactly (17/141 = 12.06% ~ '12.1%'; 5/39 = 12.8% ~ '13%'). This cross-section sourcing is stated in the affected rows.
7. Mipomersen, Phase 1 cohort sizes deliberately left NOT_REPORTED. Section 7.3.5.7 gives no n for the CS1 aPTT cohorts. The Clinical Pharmacology Review (S2 PDF p.21) gives 200 mg n=9 and 400 mg n=4 for the single-dose PK population, and states subjects continued into the multiple-dose period at the same dose, but it does not state the n for the multiple-dose aPTT analysis. Rather than assert a number the coagulation section does not contain, n_subjects is NOT_REPORTED with the context recorded in notes.
8. Warfarin DDI direction. Mipomersen slightly LOWERED peak warfarin INR (GMR 0.94, 90% CI 0.90-0.98) rather than potentiating it; the AUEC ratio was 0.99 (0.97-1.01). The 90% CI on the peak excludes unity but sits well inside the 80-125% no-effect boundary and is not bolded in the source table. Do not report this as mipomersen having an anticoagulant interaction.
9. Study-code discrepancy noted by the FDA reviewer itself. S2 PDF p.21 flags that the warfarin DDI study is numbered MIPO2900509 in the review but 'MIPO2900210' in the sponsor's clinical summary ('Clinical summary mentions this study as MIPO2900210!'). Same study, two identifiers.
10. Sequence typography. The mipomersen chemical name printed in S4 (EMA, PDF p.10) contains a run-together token 'm5CT' where every other residue is hyphen-separated. It is resolved as m5C followed by T because 'm5CT' is not a valid single residue designation and because that is the only resolution giving 20 residues and 19 internucleotide linkages, matching the document's own statement that 'mipomersen contains 19 phosphorothioate diester linkages' and the molecular formula C230H305N67O122P19S19Na19. This is a documented repair of a source typo, not an inferred sequence. Neither FDA review prints the sequence.
11. Nusinersen quality-section inconsistency. S5 PDF p.11 calls the active substance 'the sodium salt of a 18-mer 2'-O-methyl-phosphothioate oligoribonucleotide' whereas p.12 and the full chemical name give 2'-O-(2-methoxyethyl). The 2'-MOE reading is the one supported by the chemical name and the molecular formula and is what the modifications table encodes.

MODIFICATIONS TABLE. Populated for both compounds because both EMA reports publish complete per-position chemistry as an IUPAC/9CI chemical name enumerating every residue's sugar, base methylation and thio-linkage. Mipomersen: 20 rows, 5-10-5 2'-MOE/DNA/2'-MOE gapmer, 19 PS linkages, position 20 carries NOT_APPLICABLE for the 3' linkage. Nusinersen: 18 rows, uniformly 2'-MOE, 17 PS linkages, position 18 carries NOT_APPLICABLE. Nucleobases match the sequence strings letter for letter. Positions bearing 5-methyluridine (mipomersen position 4; nusinersen positions 1, 5, 6, 7, 10, 13, 16) have is_5_methyl_C false because the schema flag is specific to cytosine; the 5-methyl-U is recorded in the per-position basis text instead.

SPECIES SCOPE. Monkey aPTT data appear in this bundle (S1 section 7.3.5.7 opens with '~1.3-fold increase in aPTT' in monkeys during the first four hours; S4 PDF p.23 repeats it) and were deliberately not extracted - see refused_rows.
refused_rows:
1. MONKEY aPTT AND PLATELET DATA IN THE SAME NAMED SECTIONS. S1 section 7.3.5.7 opens with the preclinical paragraph ('changes in plasma clotting times were observed in monkeys of ~1.3-fold increase in aPTT during the first four hours after dosing ... No other clotting parameters (e.g., PT or fibrinogen) were affected'), and S4 PDF p.23 gives the same finding plus 'Monkeys treated with <= 30 mg/kg/week of mipomersen showed platelet counts approximately 30% lower than controls after about 6 months'. Quotable and locatable, but NOT extracted: this round is explicitly human-targeted, the dataset is already 1,476 animal rows against 886 human, and these monkey values are the standard mipomersen nonclinical package that animal bundles will already carry. Extracting them here would deepen exactly the imbalance this round exists to correct, and would risk duplicate animal rows. Recoverable in one grep if a curator wants them.

2. HEPARIN-INDUCED THROMBOCYTOPENIA CASE (mipomersen, S1 PDF p.~215, CS7 subject narrative). 'The patient's hospital course was complicated by heparin-induced antibody negative thrombocytopenia. After discontinuing heparin, his platelet counts improved.' Refused: the platelet fall is attributed by the narrative to heparin given during post-myocardial-infarction catheterisation, not to mipomersen. Attributing it to the oligonucleotide would be a fabrication of causality.

3. INJECTION SITE HAEMATOMA / INJECTION SITE HAEMORRHAGE (mipomersen, S1 AE tables: injection site haematoma 31.8% on mipomersen vs a lower placebo rate). Refused: these are local injection-site reactions of subcutaneous administration, tabulated by the reviewer under injection-site reactions alongside erythema and pain, and are not linked by the source to any coagulation measurement. Reporting them as bleeding outcomes attributable to a coagulation defect would misrepresent the source.

4. CONTUSION AND EPISTAXIS AE COUNTS (mipomersen, S1 Table 49 region: Contusion 7/261 (2.7%) mipomersen vs 3/129 (2.3%) placebo, under 'Injury, poisoning and procedural complications'; Epistaxis 0/261 mipomersen vs 1/129 placebo). Refused as measurement rows: the reviewer performs no bleeding-tendency analysis, the terms sit in unrelated system organ classes, and the differences are within noise. Recorded here so a curator can see they were looked at and found not to constitute a bleeding signal - which is itself weak reassurance, not a null result.

5. DRISAPERSEN THROMBOTIC CLUSTER (S3 PDF p.~113: 'nephrotic range proteinuria complicated by life-threatening thromboses and bilateral pulmonary emboli was reported in drisapersen, another phosphorothioate oligonucleotide'). Refused: this is a secondary citation about a DIFFERENT compound with no dose, no n, no timepoint and no primary source in this bundle. It is a strong lead worth chasing in the drisapersen FDA briefing document (cited by the reviewer as the November 24, 2015 Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee materials for NDA 206031) but it is not extractable data here.

6. SPINRAZA TABLE 23 CELL VALUES. The per-cell aPTT-high, aPTT-low, INR-high and INR-low shift counts exist in the review but only as pixels. Refused on the no-figure-reading rule; a placeholder row records that the data exist and are unreadable rather than letting the gap pass as silence.

7. MIPOMERSEN CS1 PER-COHORT n FOR THE aPTT ANALYSIS. The numbers 9 (200 mg) and 4 (400 mg) are available in S2 for the single-dose PK population, and it would have been easy to attach them to the multiple-dose IV aPTT rows. Refused because the source never states the n for the aPTT analysis itself, and a plausible n is still an invented n. Left NOT_REPORTED with the context in notes.

8. LUMBAR-PUNCTURE HAEMORRHAGE ROWS - EXTRACTED BUT FLAGGED, NOT REFUSED. The two nusinersen bleeding rows (5 of 173 (3%) pooled; 5 of 20 (25%) in SM201) are included, but neither regulator attributes them to a measured coagulation defect: they are procedural bleeds after failed lumbar-puncture attempts in very young infants. They are in the dataset only because the FDA used them as the stated rationale for coagulation monitoring. If the curation rule is strict attribution to a coagulation defect, both rows should be dropped, and their notes say so explicitly.

9. MIPOMERSEN PULMONARY EMBOLISM ROWS - EXTRACTED BUT FLAGGED. One event, 1/261 vs 0/129, never linked by either regulator to a coagulation measurement or a thrombophilia work-up. Included because the CHMP itself requested venous thromboembolism be counted in a CV morbidity analysis of this programme. Do not double-count the FDA row and the EMA exposure-adjusted row: they are almost certainly the same single event seen by two regulators.

10. PLATELET ROWS - EXTRACTED BUT FLAGGED. Three platelet rows are present (mipomersen pooled Phase 3, mipomersen CS5, nusinersen CS3B). Each is included only because the source itself binds the platelet result to the coagulation assessment - the mipomersen numbers are printed inside the section literally titled 'Coagulation and Platelet Issues', and the nusinersen numbers sit immediately before the named coagulation section with a single combined labelling recommendation for CBC plus coagulation testing. None is tied to a cascade readout value. Thrombocytopenia has its own dossier; a curator may drop all three without losing any clotting-cascade information.
